stem:
Omkar has line $m$ and wants a line through point $P$ parallel to $m$ by copying a corresponding angle from a transversal.

Which plan works?

options.text: Copy an angle at $P$ with no transversal that intersects line $m$, and claim the new line is parallel to $m$.
Say that the finished parallel line is what creates the transversal through $m$, instead of choosing the transversal first.
Draw a transversal through $P$ that cuts $m$, copy the corresponding angle at $P$, and draw the new line along that copied angle; it is parallel to $m$.
Use only a set-square to slide a parallel, and treat that tool method as this corresponding-angle copy hinge.

teacher.key_rationale: A transversal must cut the given line; copying the corresponding angle at $P$ makes the new line parallel to $m$. Skipping the intersecting transversal, reversing parallel and transversal, or swapping in a set-square slide all leave this hinge.
